title_en: Liu Ming v. Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the Twentieth Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways and Luo Youmin — dispute over compensation for work-related injury
keywords_en: Civil; Work-related injury compensation dispute; First instance; Second instance; Basic People's Court; Intermediate People's Court; Sichuan Province; Natural person; Legal person; Constitution; Labor Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; Subject of liability for work-related injury compensation; Validity of exculpatory clauses in contract for works; Determination of joint and several liability; Partial support; Work-related injury accident; Engineering contracting; Manual installation of bridge; Left hand disability; Labor protection; Good faith; Work-related injury
full_text_en:
Liu Ming v. The Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways, and Luo Youmin — dispute over work-related injury compensation

Plaintiff: Liu Ming, male, born on April 18, 1971, a farmer from Nanbu County, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: The Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways.

Legal Representative: Shao Huaiquan, Manager.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Zhongding, Head of the Engineering Section of the Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways.

Defendant: Luo Youmin, employee of the Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways.

Agent ad litem: Zhan Chongliang, legal worker of the Meishan County Legal Service Center, Sichuan Province.

Plaintiff Liu Ming filed a lawsuit with the Meishan County People's Court of Sichuan Province against Defendants the Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways (hereinafter referred to as the Eighth Engineering Company) and Luo Youmin over a dispute concerning work-related injury compensation.

Plaintiff’s Allegations: I worked at the construction site of the two defendants and suffered a work-related accident that resulted in the disability of my left hand. I request that the court order the two defendants to jointly compensate me for lost wages of RMB 6,000, hospitalization subsistence allowance of RMB 250, appraisal fee of RMB 450, transportation expenses of RMB 1,500, disability subsistence allowance of RMB 12,000, and costs for further medical treatment; the litigation costs shall be borne by the defendants.

Defendants’ Defense: The plaintiff violated safety operation regulations and caused the work-related injury; therefore, we do not agree to compensate.

The Meishan County People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On August 27, 1998, the Meishan 106 Line Project Department of the Defendant Eighth Engineering Company entered into an engineering contract with its employee, Defendant Luo Youmin, stipulating that Luo Youmin would contract the installation of the roadway slabs of the Xilaiyan Bridge on the Meishan 106 Line, with a total project price of over RMB 260,000, on a lump-sum basis. The contract also provided that Luo Youmin would be responsible for any injuries, deaths, or disabilities occurring during construction. After the contract was signed, Luo Youmin organized migrant workers to carry out the installation.

On September 2 of the same year, Plaintiff Liu Ming was introduced to work for Defendant Luo Youmin. To prevent work-related injuries, Luo Youmin had called a meeting of the migrant workers to emphasize safety issues, requiring them to use iron hooks when placing rubber pads under the slabs to prevent the slabs from falling and causing injury. At approximately 6:00 p.m. on October 6, Liu Ming, while placing rubber pads under the slabs, did not use iron hooks and directly used his hands. Due to the slipping of the jack supporting the slab, a slab weighing over 10 tons fell, crushing Liu Ming’s left hand. Luo Youmin immediately sent Liu Ming to the hospital for 21 days of inpatient treatment. The medical expenses, nursing fees, transportation costs, meal expenses during Liu Ming’s hospitalization, and post-discharge treatment costs, totaling RMB 5,308.91, were all borne by Luo Youmin.

On March 5, 1999, the Forensic Technical Office of the Leshan Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province conducted an appraisal of Liu Ming’s injuries, concluding: Liu Ming sustained fractures of the third and fourth metacarpal bones of the left hand, comminuted fractures of the proximal phalanges of the index and middle fingers, dislocation of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the index finger; after undergoing amputation of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the left index finger and internal fixation surgery with steel pins on the second and third metacarpal bones of the left hand, the flexion and extension function of the left middle finger was completely lost, with a disability grade of Level 7 for work-related injuries.

The average annual wage of workers in the Meishan area of Sichuan Province in 1998 was RMB 5,014.

It was also found that the installation of the roadway slabs of the Xilaiyan Bridge on the Meishan 106 Line, whether from the perspective of the site environment or the technology and equipment of the construction unit, allowed for the use of cranes to directly hoist and install the slabs. Although the use of manual installation could reduce costs, it increased safety risks.

The Meishan County People's Court held:

Article 42, Paragraph 2 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China provides: "The state creates conditions for employment through various channels, strengthens labor protection, improves working conditions, and, on the basis of expanding production, increases remuneration for work and welfare benefits." Article 3 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China provides that workers have the right to occupational safety and health protection. Article 4 provides: "Employers shall establish and improve rules and regulations in accordance with the law to ensure that workers enjoy their labor rights and perform their labor obligations." Defendant Luo Youmin, as the contractor of the slab installation project for the Xilaiyan Bridge on the Meishan 106 Line, after recruiting Plaintiff Liu Ming to work on the project, formed a labor contract relationship between the parties. As the project contractor and employer, Luo Youmin bore the responsibility for the labor protection of the migrant workers in accordance with the law. The manual installation of bridge roadway slabs itself carried a high degree of danger. To this end, Luo Youmin should have taken corresponding safety measures and provided on-site supervision and guidance. However, Luo Youmin only verbally emphasized safety before the work and failed to pay adequate attention, resulting in Liu Ming’s safety accident. Although Liu Ming also had the fault of violating safety operation rules during the construction, he was not a professional railway construction worker and his violation was relatively minor; therefore, Luo Youmin’s civil liability could not be exempted.

China has always attached great importance to strengthening labor protection. Defendant Eighth Engineering Company, as the construction enterprise for the Xilaiyan Bridge on the Meishan 106 Line, had the conditions to adopt a less risky working method for the installation of roadway slabs. However, in order to reduce costs, it contracted the work to an individual, using manual installation, thereby increasing the safety risks for the workers. The contract entered into between the company and Defendant Luo Youmin contained a clause stating that "Luo Youmin shall be responsible for any injuries, deaths, or disabilities occurring during construction," thereby shifting the safety risks that only an enterprise could bear to a natural person with limited capacity. This clause infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of workers and violated the relevant provisions of the Constitution and the Labor Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 58, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, this clause shall be deemed invalid and not protected by law. The Eighth Engineering Company shall, in accordance with the law, bear joint and several liability for the work-related injury accident of Plaintiff Liu Ming.

Article 98 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Citizens enjoy the right to life and health." After Plaintiff Liu Ming’s left hand was disabled due to the work-related injury, his request for an order that the two defendants jointly compensate him for lost wages, hospitalization subsistence allowance, and disability subsistence allowance is consistent with Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and shall be supported. Liu Ming’s request that the two defendants pay for further medical expenses, as the fact of further medical treatment has not yet occurred, means that such expenses are in an uncertain state and will not be adjudicated in this case; Liu Ming may file a separate claim after the fact of further medical treatment occurs.

In summary, the Meishan County People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 18, 1999:

1. Within five days after this judgment takes effect, Defendant Luo Youmin shall pay Plaintiff Liu Ming a total of RMB 18,679.56 for medical expenses, lost wages, hospitalization subsistence allowance, nursing fees, transportation expenses, disability compensation, and disability employment compensation (RMB 5,308.15 of which has already been paid and shall be deducted during execution).

2. Defendant the Eighth Engineering Company of the Second Engineering Division of the 20th Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways shall bear joint and several liability for the above amounts.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 757.18 and appraisal fee of RMB 450 shall be borne by Luo Youmin.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Plaintiff Liu Ming appealed, arguing that the original judgment did not address the issue of further medical expenses and that other compensation items were insufficient. He requested that the judgment be amended to increase further medical expenses, lost wages, and other items, and to order the payment of back wages.

During the second-instance trial, the Meishan Area Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province, in addition to affirming the facts regarding the work-related injury found at first instance, also found that: during Liu Ming’s 21-day hospitalization, the appellee Luo Youmin paid medical expenses, hospitalization fees, transportation expenses, and other costs totaling RMB 6,457.71. In addition to the amounts already paid by Luo Youmin, the losses suffered by Liu Ming due to the work-related injury included: lost wages after discharge of RMB 1,500, further medical expenses of RMB 2,000 (including hospitalization medical fees, lost wages, nutrition fees, nursing fees, etc.), disability compensation of RMB 5,014, disability employment compensation of RMB 6,254, and other losses of RMB 2,443, all of which remained unpaid. In addition, the appellee Eighth Engineering Company still owed Liu Ming wages of RMB 1,033 for September 1998.

The Meishan Area Intermediate People's Court held that the appellant Liu Ming was disabled due to a work-related injury and that the two appellees should bear compensation liability. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 155 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Meishan Area Intermediate People's Court conducted mediation, and the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement on May 17, 1999:

In addition to the RMB 6,457.71 already paid by the appellee Luo Youmin, the appellee Eighth Engineering Company shall pay a lump sum of RMB 18,244 to the appellant Liu Ming before May 30, 1999, for lost wages after discharge, disability compensation, disability employment compensation, further medical expenses, other losses, and back wages.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 757.18 and appraisal fee of RMB 450 for the first instance, and court acceptance fee of RMB 757.18 for the second instance, totaling RMB 1,964.36, shall be borne by the Eighth Engineering Company.
